rationale: The Old English verb *a-driógan* means "to endure, suffer, or put up with" hardship or something unpleasant, which aligns directly with digest.v.03 ("put up with something or somebody unpleasant"). The context from Bosworth-Toller and the Boethius attestation (Bt. 40, 3) consistently reflects this sense of tolerating or enduring adversity, not physical carrying or birthing.
